notes: Account profile: mid-market SaaS platform for B2B knowledge search + support automation. Heavy tails on long docs (avg doc 8k tokens).
Primary ask: migrate from OpenAI -> Redwood Hosted for quick win, then Dedicated for predictable cost & residency.
Technical constraints: must preserve prompt parity for support summarization workflows (legal reviews rely on exact truncation behavior), streaming chunk semantics important for UX.
POC setup: created identical eval harness (same prompts, stop tokens, temperature). Baseline provider = OpenAI gpt-4o-doc; Redwood served vicuna-finetuned variant in hosted mode.

Observed regressions: summarization ROUGE-L down 9-12% on canonical set; hallucination rate on long docs increased for >4k token inputs. Need A/B to identify whether model variant, tokenization, or prompt truncation causes gap.

Compat layer notes: customer engineering prefers a small middleware that translates OpenAI-style function-calls -> Redwood structured output; also normalizes streaming events (chunk ids, delta text) and maps stop tokens. SE recommended: header mapping + response envelope shim + token-metering comparator.

Performance: hosted API latency ~120-180ms per token streamed vs baseline ~90-140ms; initial batching config increased throughput but slightly worsened tail latency — concern for real-time chat use-case.

Security/legal: Data residency required for EU customers; Redwood hosted EU region acceptable for phase 1. For Dedicated they want VPC + bring-your-own-KMS. Legal drafting DPA addendum; purchase team needs residency text clarified.
Customer quote: "We love the control promises — but regressions are blockers. If parity is proven, Dedicated sizing and a 12-month commit are likely."
SE action items: create conversion shim repo (example middleware), add tokenization parity tests, surface model suggestions (quantized variants) and batching profiles from Redwood Optimize.
Commercial notes: preliminary ARR estimate 50–150k; asked for committed QPS and STU (streaming token units) based pricing examples. Wants discount schedule tied to commit size.
